title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
exercise: Name 5 things you can see, 4 things you can touch, 3 things you can hear, 2 things you can smell, and 1 thing you can taste. This pulls attention back to the present moment.

title: Thought Record
exercise: Write down the thought bothering you. Then ask: what's the evidence for it? What's the evidence against it? Is there a more balanced way to see this situation?

title: Behavioral Activation
exercise: Pick one small, achievable activity you used to enjoy (even a 5-minute version of it) and schedule it for today. Mood often follows action, not the other way around.

title: STOP Technique
exercise: Stop. Take a breath. Observe what you're feeling and thinking. Proceed with a choice rather than a reaction.

title: Worry Time
exercise: Set aside a specific 10-minute window later today to fully worry about this. When the worry comes up now, note it down and tell yourself you'll address it in your worry window.

title: Box Breathing
exercise: Breathe in for 4 counts, hold for 4, breathe out for 4, hold for 4. Repeat 4 times. This activates your body's relaxation response.

title: Values Check-In
exercise: Write down one value that matters to you (connection, growth, honesty, etc.) and one small action today that would align with it, however small.

title: Reframe Exercise
exercise: Take the critical thought you're having about yourself. Now write down what you'd say to a close friend who told you they felt this way about themselves.
